title: The ninth: Arafah
hook: standing on the plain from noon to sunset: Hajj is Arafah (Tirmidhi)

segments.voice: Yesterday: the eighth, five prayers and a night in the tents at Mina. Your line: a city of tents.

A group of travelers arrives at the plain of Arafah and finds the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ there. They have one question: what is the Hajj? A man is sent to call out his answer to the crowd, and it's short. The Hajj is Arafah. The report, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Ya'mar, is in the collection of Tirmidhi. The cloths, the circling, the walking, the tents: all of it leads to this one day. Today, the ninth.
screen: `TRAVELERS WITH ONE QUESTION.` → `WHAT IS THE HAJJ?` → `THE HAJJ IS ARAFAH.`

segments.voice: First, the word. Wuquf means standing, and it's the name for being present on the plain of Arafah on the ninth day. You met this day from home back on day one hundred twenty-eight; today, the plain itself. Tirmidhi's report goes on: whoever reaches Arafah before dawn after that night has caught the Hajj. Miss it, and in the teaching of the scholars the Hajj itself is missed, whatever else was done. Second, what the Prophet did. Jabir's account in Sahih Muslim says he left Mina after sunrise, and when the sun passed its height, he addressed the people; then the noon and afternoon prayers were prayed together. Then he rode to the place of standing, faced the qiblah, and stayed there, still on his camel, until the sun had set. Noon to sunset: that's the shape of the day. Third, what standing means. It doesn't require being on your feet. Pilgrims sit under umbrellas, stand by the roadside, rest in tents, lift their hands, read the Qur'an, cry, say nothing at all. The rite is being there, turned toward God, for those hours. Fourth, why this day. Aisha reports, in Sahih Muslim, the Prophet saying that there is no day on which Allah sets free more servants from the Fire than the day of Arafah. So the plain fills with people asking, for themselves, for their parents, for names written on scraps of paper by people at home. At sunset the whole crowd moves at once. Surah two gives the instruction for that moment, in Pickthall's words: "But, when ye press on in the multitude from 'Arafat, remember Allah by the sacred monument." That's where tomorrow begins.
screen: `WUQUF: STANDING, BEING THERE.` · `FROM NOON TO SUNSET.` · `ON YOUR FEET OR NOT.` · `NO DAY FREES MORE SERVANTS.`

segments.voice: Stand, or sit if standing is hard, and turn your palms up; pilgrims give a whole afternoon to this, and a few minutes is a real start. If you pray, ask in your own words for yourself and then for someone else by name; if not, hold in mind what you most hope for, and one person you hope it for too.
Wuquf. Standing on the plain of Arafah, from noon to sunset on the ninth, the heart of the Hajj. Today's word.
Your line: hajj is arafah. One afternoon of being there is the heart of it all. See you at Muzdalifah.

howItsDone: On the ninth of Dhul-Hijjah, pilgrims go from Mina to the plain of Arafah, pray the noon and afternoon prayers together, and spend the afternoon until sunset in du'a, recitation and remembrance before moving on to Muzdalifah.

chat.says: Does a pilgrim have to stay on their feet all afternoon at Arafah?
options: No. Wuquf means being present, turned to God; sitting or resting counts.
Yes. If they sit down even once before sunset, their whole Hajj is lost.
No, they can skip Arafah if they circle the Ka'ba extra times instead.
chat.meaning: Wuquf means standing, but it doesn't require being on your feet. The rite is being on the plain, turned toward God, for those hours.

notes: Tirmidhi 889 (Abd al-Rahman ibn Ya'mar: people of Najd asked; 'the Hajj is Arafah'; whoever comes before dawn on the night of Jam' has caught it): confirm number and grading. The report calls them people of Najd; the script says 'a group of travelers'.
'Miss it, and in the teaching of the scholars the Hajj itself is missed': standard fiqh; confirm phrasing.
Sahih Muslim 1218 (Jabir: sermon after the sun declined, zuhr and asr together, then standing facing the qiblah until sunset): confirm.
Sahih Muslim 1348 (Aisha: no day on which Allah frees more servants from the Fire than the day of Arafah): paraphrased; confirm.
Pickthall 2:198 quoted from memory, including the spelling 'Arafat: confirm exact wording.
'Names written on scraps of paper by people at home' and the list of how pilgrims spend the afternoon: general color; check.
